The authors established this dataset themselves, which matches the figshare_stroke description of stroke patient EEG data.

ref_extractions.title: MSHANet: A Multiscale Hybrid Attention Network for Motor Imagery EEG Decoding
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper proposes MSHANet for MI-EEG decoding but only evaluates on BCI Competition IV Datasets 2a and 2b, and EEGMMID - all healthy subject datasets. There is no mention of stroke patients or the figshare_stroke dataset. The paper mentions clinical applications and stroke in the introduction as motivation, but does not actually use any stroke patient data.

ref_extractions.title: Heterogeneous transfer learning model for improving the classification performance of fNIRS signals in motor imagery among cross-subject stroke patients
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper focuses on fNIRS (functional near-infrared spectroscopy) signals, not EEG. While it involves stroke patients and motor imagery, it uses EEG data from healthy individuals as a source domain for transfer learning to fNIRS data from stroke patients. The target modality is fNIRS, not EEG, and there is no mention of the figshare_stroke EEG dataset. The paper explicitly states it uses 'labeled electroencephalogram (EEG) data from healthy individuals as the source domain' and 'two MI-fNIRS datasets from eight stroke patients' - these are fNIRS datasets, not the figshare_stroke EEG dataset.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Uses fNIRS data from stroke patients, not EEG; source domain is EEG from healthy individuals; no mention of figshare_stroke dataset; heterogeneous transfer from EEG to fNIRS modalities

ref_extractions.title: Dynamic graph attention network based on multi-scale frequency domain features for motion imagery decoding in hemiplegic patients
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper focuses on hemiplegic patients (which includes stroke patients) but explicitly states it validated on 'the public PhysioNet dataset' - not the figshare_stroke dataset. The paper discusses stroke rehabilitation applications but uses a different public dataset (PhysioNet). There is no mention of figshare or the specific stroke patient EEG dataset. The within-subject accuracy of 61.6% and cross-subject of 52.7% are reported on PhysioNet data.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Validated on public PhysioNet dataset only; no mention of figshare_stroke dataset; mentions hemiplegic patients and stroke rehabilitation as application domain but uses different data source

ref_extractions.title: Mutual Generation for Cross-domain Challenge in Stroke Patients' Motor Imagery Classification and Functional Recovery Prediction
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper explicitly uses stroke patient MI-EEG data and mentions 'The Huashan Stroke MI dataset was collected at Huashan Hospital'. It describes two MI-EEG datasets of stroke patients performing motor imagery tasks with left-and right-handed MI classification. However, this appears to be a different dataset (Huashan Stroke MI dataset, collected at Huashan Hospital, Fudan University) rather than the figshare_stroke dataset. The paper focuses on cross-domain challenges between different hemiplegic sides and functional recovery prediction. While highly related to stroke patient MI-EEG, it does not explicitly mention figshare or the specific dataset identifier 21679035.

ref_extractions.super_meta_note: Different dataset: Huashan Stroke MI dataset from Huashan Hospital, not figshare_stroke; but very similar population and task

ref_extractions.title: Integrating EEG Artifact Removal with Deep Learning for Accurate Motor Imagery Classification in Acute Stroke
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper explicitly describes using EEG data from 50 acute stroke patients from Xuanwu Hospital, Capital Medical University, Beijing, performing left- and right-hand motor imagery tasks. The dataset description matches the figshare_stroke dataset characteristics: 50 acute stroke patients, 32-channel semi-dry EEG system (ZhenTec NT1), 500 Hz sampling, left/right hand MI tasks, 40 trials per participant, within 1-30 days post-stroke. The paper defines a concrete binary classification task using CNN, LSTM, and hybrid CNN-LSTM models. The citation [28] in the paper likely refers to the figshare dataset source. This strongly matches the known figshare_stroke dataset (21679035) which has 50 stroke patients with left/right hand MI.
ref_extractions.epoch_params: ICA-based artifact removal with MARA, SASICA, EMAR; filtering and re-referencing; .edf files with motor imagery event information
ref_extractions.label_mapping: binary: left hand MI vs right hand MI
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: 50 acute stroke patients from Xuanwu Hospital, Beijing; 32-channel ZhenTec NT1 at 500 Hz; left/right hand MI tasks; 40 trials per participant; 1-30 days post-stroke; explicit comparison of CNN, LSTM, hybrid CNN-LSTM for binary classification; matches figshare_stroke dataset description

feasibility_reason: The dataset contains clear event structure with trial_type values 1 and 2 mapping to left hand and right hand motor imagery respectively, along with phase markers (instruction, MI beginning, break) in the value column. This supports a standard 2-class motor imagery classification task. The events.tsv sample confirms alternating left/right trials with consistent timing structure.

event_annotations.notes: Event IDs 1, 2, 3 are defined in task-motor-imagery_events.json with explicit level mappings: '1'='Instruction beginning', '2'='Motor imagery beginning', '3'='Break beginning'. The events.tsv file confirms these appear as alternating trial phases with durations 2000ms (instruction/break) and 4000ms (motor imagery), matching the 8s trial structure (2s instruction + 4s MI + 2s break) × 40 trials = 320s total duration per EDF file. The MAT files (eeg.label with values 1/2) encode trial_type (left/right hand imagery), not the event IDs 1-3 which represent phase onsets. Stimulus files confirm: stim1.png=instruction, stim2.mp4=motor imagery, stim3.png=break. No event annotations were detected in EDF headers; events are external markers.

_dropped_candidates.reason: The 4-class MI paradigm with forward arm raise/lower and lateral arm raise/lower is described in two references (10.1016/j.jneumeth.2026.110707), but these explicitly state a different dataset from China Rehabilitation Research Center with only 24 subjects and 12 subjects per forward/lateral group. The super_meta_note confirms this is NOT the figshare_stroke dataset. The figshare_stroke dataset has only 2-class left/right hand MI per its own events.json, events.tsv, and MAT file labels. No 4-class event IDs exist in the grounded catalog.

_dropped_candidates.paradigm: phase state detection (instruction vs MI vs break)
_dropped_candidates.reason: While event IDs 1/2/3 represent instruction/MI/break phases, these are trial phase markers per the locked meanings, not discriminable task labels. No reference proposes classifying these phases as the primary task. The actual MI task uses trial_type (1/2) as class labels during the MI phase. Creating a phase-detection task would be manufacturing a task not grounded in references or dataset purpose.
